There isn't -- there isn't interpretation from me or anyone else about the contents of what's here. There may be one or two small exceptions. But in that -- in that -- those exceptions may be where there was already a summary that was written of the intercept itself. So really these are -- they are excerpts, extracts, of quotes from the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this -- this first one, right on the list there, 19th January, 1995, could you tell us whether or not, if you are aware if there is a notebook or an operator identified with respect to that particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a notebook associated with it. There is a printout associated with it, an electronic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not an operator has been identified with respect to that intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, someone has been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you participate in trying to ascertain who the operator was that transcribed that or is related to that intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was done by other members of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the content of the summary itself, you've indicated that that's derived from the intercept itself?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's based upon obviously a translation of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is the purpose of that to assist the reader in going through the -- the intercept --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- material?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might mention, I think the Court may already know, but for example, just in glancing down at the fifth -- at the fifth row where it says X and then in parentheses it says, "Zivanovic" and then it says Y and then in parentheses it says "Pantic," this is where an operator would have probably recognised the voices but wasn't certain and therefore indicated the names in parentheses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that based on your understanding of how the operators in fact worked?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The nature of the operation itself?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to take you to another area, if I could. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether or not that, in fact, occurs with respect to the intercepts that are contained within the binder collection?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you approximate how many times you have noted that that has occurred?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I just want to take a look at a few of those just so that the Court has an idea of what it is you are talking about. The first one I'd like to look at, if I could, is -- could I have 65 ter 1182 brought up on e-court? And could I have P02367 brought up on e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1182A, B, C or D?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 1182A, B, C or D, good question. 1182B, please. And then I think B also with respect to 2367. I don't know if it's possible to have both of those...

utterances.text: Is it possible or not? I'm told it's not. We can put one on the ELMO, if you have it available, and one on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, actually, Mr. President, I was going to -- I was going to see if the witness could actually display them both, since it involves some comparison, which I think would be helpful for the Court to follow. utterances.text: Do you need Madam Usher's assistance?

utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Okay. So both of these conversations record that they were picked up on frequency 255.850, and the times as we just discussed are five minutes off. On the e-court version of that conversation, from the northern site, it says Burtula didn't respect the order of the boss, didn't follow the order of the boss. And I can come back to that. I mean it's a little similar to the last conversation also. Point 3 says -- is similar, is -- is almost -- is identical. Almost identical. That he needs 30 people as it was ordered. The fourth point says to take them from Nastic on -- on the version on e-court it says -- gives the name of Nasic. And then the next -- the next one, point 5, comes through on the -- on the e-court part way down, and again there are -- the words are identical. And the sixth point also, "I'll have to move everything -- I'll disturb everything in his direction if I pull them out. And a lot is depending on him." And that's the same sentence, the last sentence on e-court version of the document is identical. And then the rest of that conversation was not recorded by that operator at the northern site at the division. utterances.text: All right. Ms. Frease, could you tell us about -- could you tell us about these two comparisons, that's between the 9.55 conversation and the 9. -- I'm sorry, the 10.00 conversation?

utterances.text: The 9.57. This one is the 9.57 and the 10.00 conversation. This is the third version of it, which was recorded at the northern site by the 2 Corps unit. I'm telling you in all seriousness, I still have 3500 parcels to deliver and I don't have a solution."

utterances.text: With respect to this intercept, as concerns the differences between them, did you make -- did you evaluate whether or not the differences between them substantively changed the meaning or the content of the communication in question?

utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I'd like to start with the one on the right. Well, just both of them. We're looking at the -- at the conversations at 1627, and they were both taken from frequency 251.675. utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In evaluating the two intercepts, would it be fair to say, in your opinion, that the summarised version of the conversation carries the same import as the verbatim version of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to the three that -- that you just testified to involving conversation, a purported conversation between Beara and Krstic, did you have occasion to notice whether or not one intercept operator, for example, may have missed the introduction or another intercept operator actually got it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that an unusual occurrence with respect to your evaluation of the intercepts that are used -- that have been used in this collection?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that one of the tools that you used in order to evaluate the reliability of the information or what was conveyed in the conversation?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, some of the differences that you have highlighted for the Court have been -- well, I would say rather evident, clear. And that those are points where they were incongruous. Is there an explanation that you can offer with respect to why two intercept operators listening apparently to the same conversation write down completely different words?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could be several explanations. Depending on the words that they wrote down, sometimes the words sound very similar. They could have -- there could have been more static that someone else was picking up. They could have been listening different -- listening to it a different amount of times. One may have listened to the conversation more times than another, and therefore has been more accurate. It's hard to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I take it you don't have any first-hand knowledge of that. Is that fair to say? As to the circumstances that would explain --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- the differences?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, you can put it differently. I'll put it myself: Did you ever discuss this with the various intercept operators or with some of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what did they tell you? How would they account for the differences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just like that, that they just could have heard it wrong. One pops into my mind where there is a conversation with someone nicknamed Nidjo, and later on in the conversation it says, "Hey Mico." They sound very similar. It doesn't make sense that that name -- that that nickname would have come in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm being told that we can't go on for two hours without a break, and that's because of exigencies and arrangements that exist here. What I suggest is that we give Ms. Frease also a short break and allow the rest of the group to make the necessary arrangements so that we can then continue up until 7.00. So we will have between 10 and 15 minutes' break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. --- Break taken at 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, I think we left off and I had been asking you some questions about the differences that you found between these simultaneously captured intercepted communications. Could I ask you just -- in evaluating the differences that you found, did you find that the import of the conversations had changed in any way as a result of those differences? In other words, was the conversation materially affected, in your mind, based upon those differences?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't think of any -- where I thought there was a material difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible for me to have the transcript on the screen? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you find that aside from these differences, that you didn't believe or find to be material, that the simultaneously captured intercepts were materially consistent?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could, I would just like to bring your attention to a different area. And in particular, I wanted to draw your attention to an intercept captured at 10.09 on the 13th of July. And I think I can have it brought up on e-court. The 65 ter number is 1130. I think the English and B/C/S version should be displayed; that would be A and B. If you need to see the typewritten version to make it easier to read, just let me know and we could have that done as well. I don't believe the pages correspond that are in e-court right now, but is it possible to go forward on the page on the right? That is ERN 0080-0808. I think you may have to go forward another page.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's back one page, actually, to 810.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you could go back. All right. Thank you. First, do you recognise this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And have you had an opportunity to look at it and evaluate it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this intercept in particular, there is an indication that there is a conversation that involves someone -- well, appears to be a Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Somebody by the name of Lucic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And somebody by the name of Zoka?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us a little bit about this intercept, and have you looked at it in terms of seeking out corroboration or trying to make a judgement as to its reliability?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us what about this intercept you looked at?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, aside from looking at the general context, I looked at it also in relation to overhead imagery that was taken on the 13th of July at 2.00. And this conversation was recorded at 10.00 in the morning and indicates that there were 400 -- they're referred to here as Balija, which is a derogatory term for Muslims, who have shown up in Konjevic Polje and that they should be put on the playground, and lined up in four or five -- in four to five rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the reference to the playground, did you form an opinion as to what that was referring to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the soccer field. I believe it refers to the soccer field in Nova Kasaba, which is down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Was that the subject of the photograph that you previously indicated?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, that was 65 ter 1662 and 1663. Previously indicated in the record. Okay. Now, you said that there is an indication in the conversation with respect to people being lined up. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, that appears to be, at least from the conversation, a statement that is attributed to Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this particular intercept, did you obtain or become aware of other corroboration with respect to prisoners being lined up in a soccer field?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just tell us what that information was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- being lined up specifically on the soccer field, there are -- there's a conversation at 1602 on that same day about a larger group of -- I think it's 1.000 or 1500 men that have been gathered together. There are also the couple of intercepts at 1400 and 1405 on that same day that correspond to a telegram that we discussed before about troops that should be patrolling that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me just refer you -- if I could have 65 ter 1142, please, displayed on e-court. If I could just refer you to this intercept. That's 1142A and B, for the record. Just to bring to the Court's attention, this document has a signature at its base, and I think I'm rather concerned about broadcast with respect to the signature. I don't know if there is a way to size the window so that we can avoid a showing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. We will do that before we broadcast, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Frease, do you recognise this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The signatures, the names are still coming up on my screen. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, they are. I don't believe we're broadcasting though at this time.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both documents; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed because otherwise we're going to waste too much time. Let's not broadcast any of these and go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the 1602 conversation that you referred to --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- previously?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this conversation you indicated that there was reference to a number of people that were in a stadium in Kasaba; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that what you interpreted to be the playground?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now there is an indication here of a person named Malinic.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the -- he was the commander of the 65th Protection Regiments, military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know whom, if anybody, he reported to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reported to his commander who was Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've indicated previously that there is a reference to a telegram with respect, bearing upon the -- these particular people that are in the stadium; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Could I have 65 ter 0192, please, on e-court. Okay. Now, is this the order you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there is indication of 1400 hours at the top of it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what is that a reference to, if you could tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an order that was written by the commander of the 65th Protection Regiment, Lieutenant-Colonel Milomir Savcic and it's an order to the commander of the military police battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment. It's also addressed to General Mladic and to General Gvero, not by name but by position for their information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is the commander of the military police battalion of the 65th, who is that person?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Zoran Malinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And this telegram relates to, it says, a thousand members of the former 28th captured in -- it says Dusanova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that Nova Kasaba that you've indicated previously?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You also indicated that there was a mention of this telegram in a separate intercept; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know offhand what intercept that was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at 14.05 on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I please have P02362 displayed on e-court. A and B, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That doesn't...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. On the English version I think -- I think we need to go back to the first page. I think.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This the only page in e-court. There is only one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not broadcasting, are we? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Looks like we're having some difficulty finding the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to read the B/C/S version of this?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Is there an indication with respect to a telegram or an order in this B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it is --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- if you see it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's five lines down. X is speaking. But the -- the second line in the -- the second line in the conversation refers to the football pitch, the football field. And then five lines down where X is speaking, he is saying to his sort of buddy, "Don't accept anyone. I'll -- I'm going to send you a telegram, an urgent telegram now. Don't -- don't accept anyone. I'll send you the telegram right now and explain -- and explain everything or explain things. Provide security, secure it well and you'll get the telegram now."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, is there an indication on this intercept as to the time that this conversation is alleged to have occurred?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at 1405.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall the time that was indicated on the order?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you consider that in terms of evaluating the reliability of not only this intercept, but the one previously at 1009?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the -- the intercept at 1009 also mentioned a man named Lucic that Colonel Beara addressed and he is a member of -- Pavle Lucic is a member of the 65th Protection Regiment. It's the 2nd Motorised Brigade, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Motorised battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could move you to a slightly different area. And that relates to additional corroboration you did with respect to some of the intercepts in this particular case. What I would like to have is -- on e-court is 65 ter 1187. And I think we can have A and B shown on e-court. And that relates to an intercept purportedly occurring at 1111 on 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. First -- all right. First, do you recognise this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have an opportunity to evaluate the reliability of the information that's contained in this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular, can you tell us what it is that you focused on and what it is you were able to establish in terms of corroborative evidence?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general subject matter of the intercept, which has to do with -- first it's a -- it's a conversation between Colonel Ljubo Beara and Cerovic, who was the assistant commander for morale and religious affairs, I believe it is, at the Drina Corps, and X. And Cerovic is saying that triage has to be done today on the -- and then you'll see there are a few dots and question marks, but if you go down to the fifth line, it says, "Triage has to be done on the prisoners." And then X, who is the other participant in that conversation with Cerovic at the beginning says that Colonel Beara is here, and then further down in the conversation it -- Cerovic says that he's received instructions from above to do triage on those, and then he's interrupted and Beara says that he doesn't want to talk about it on the phone. So it is the general subject matter of triage being done on the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And were you able to determine whether or not there was legitimacy to what was being discussed in this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to corroborative material, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what corroborative material, if any you found, in relation to the triage of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: An entry in a duty officer's logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 0377 please shown on e-court. Okay. With respect to the B/C/S version, I think we will find the entry on page 146, and with respect to the English translation, we will find the entry on page 27. Thank you. Could I just direct your attention to time indicated, 1115. First of all, do you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what is it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an excerpt from the duty officer's logbook from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And let me direct your attention to 1115. Can you tell us what, if anything, you found in terms of entries at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entry says, "It was reported from Zlatar that triage of wounded and prisoners must be carried out (it was reported to Beara)."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In your view, was that corroborative of the intercept which occurred at 1111 on the same day?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, do you know anything about who made the entry in the duty officer's logbook on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- the duty officer that day was Trbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know -- well, let me ask you, do you know Trbic's first name?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I -- it escapes me right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know what Trbic's position was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the security detail at the -- at the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you tell us how you know who made that entry on that date?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- from people in the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me refer you to a different entry in the duty officer's logbook. And that's at page 148 in the B/C/S version, and page 29 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- with respect to the -- to the entries and who was the duty officer, on that day there are a handful of intercepts that refer to that person having been the duty officer as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Why don't we have a look at this one and maybe if time permits we might be able to get back to that one. I would like to direct your attention first to the entry at 1400 hours with respect to this particular document. Have you seen that before?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers -- well, what it says is that Popovic requested a bus with a full tank of 500 litres of D2 diesel, and that the Zlatar duty officer and Golic were informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is this information corroborative of intercepts that you have evaluated or looked at in the collection offered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall off the top of your head what those intercepts were?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was -- it's an intercept at 1358 on the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have, please, P02454 displayed in e-court. A and B, please.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a different day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with us for a moment. I'm sorry. Bear with us for just a moment. I apologise. All right. We have a misidentification of that particular intercept, so let me just move on and maybe we can revisit it.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you referring to the index?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us what's on the index.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you kindly. Okay. It's at the base of the document on the right, if you could scroll down, I guess, or up. All right. Do you recognise this intercept, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that the intercept that you were referring to previously?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And this is a reference to a request for 500 litres of D2 diesel fuel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Is this what you found corroborative of the -- I should phrase it the other way. Did you find the duty officer's entry corroborative of this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are there any other intercepts that you found corroborative of this particular order?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but we found a fuel log that -- that also -- that further corroborates this and the duty officer's log entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the fuel -- fuel log, you said?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is that a document that -- that is a part of your authentication binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Just for the record, that was in the authentication binder, which is 65 ter 1074, and it was located -- and P02127, located at page 66 and 67 of that document. I just want to refer you, I think, to one other area and that relates to page 85 of your authentication binder in particular. Now, that -- if I could have in e-court is 65 ter 1074. I think on document on the -- on the left-hand side, if we could page forward, we will find the precise intercept that is the subject of the corroboration.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to go forward in the document on the left to page 86, which is 0603-0160. Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the intercept on the right is from the previous conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well. Now, with respect to the document on the left, there is a time that's indicated of 1458 hours. It is an intercept of X and Y; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you consider this intercept in evaluating the reliability of the collection of intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what about this specific intercept you considered and whether or not you were able to corroborate the information that's contained in it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well it -- it starts off, and very quickly you see that it refers to some sort of a report. But what was interesting about this was trying -- was to see whether we had a report that corresponded to these points and these locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you find such a report?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I have please page -- I believe it's page 91 of the same document shown. That is ERN 0603-0165. Now, Ms. Frease, do you recognise what's displayed on e-court?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you've indicated that you found corroboration for the reference to Petkovici, Baljkovica, and Memici?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us where in this document -- first of all, tell us what the document is and tell us where in the document you found corroboration of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll down a little bit more? What this is -- oops, sorry. I said that too soon. Can you go back up? Thanks. It is a -- an interim combat report that was written on the 18th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that the same date as the intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it came from the command of the Zvornik Brigade. So then if you could scroll down a little bit, please. You see point 2, there are few paragraphs in this report, paragraph 1, paragraph 2, paragraph 3, actually indicated with numbers, number 1, number 2, number 3. So after number 2, then at the bottom of that point or paragraph you see the references to Petkovci-Baljkovica-Memici front-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That is in the last sentence of point 2 as indicated on this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's what's specifically referred to in the intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And based upon that -- let me ask you, can you consider that in evaluating the reliability of this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the next topic you're going to deal with can be resolved in three, four minutes, okay; otherwise, we adjourn.

utterances.text: I think it might be wise to adjourn. I don't really think it will take more than 10, 15 minutes, but...

utterances.text: She still has to -- Ms. Frease still has to return for cross-examination.
